newsitem.title: USA: Basin Electric sees 550 MW Wyo. coal unit up Wed.
newsitem.headline: Basin Electric sees 550 MW Wyo. coal unit up Wed.

text.p: Basin Electric Power Cooperative's Laramie River Station (LRS) unit 3 was expected to return to service Wednesday after being shut Saturday for unplanned boiler tube repairs, the utility said on Monday.
"It will take until Wednesday morning to bring it back," said spokesman Stan Stelter.

The problem at LRS 3 was discovered while crews were repairng the boiler tubes in the facility's unit 2, he said. LRS 2, which was shut last Friday, began its restart today, Stelter said. "It's starting to go back on line."
He added LRS's unit 1 was operating at full output.
The three LRS units, located in Wheatland, Wyo., each are rated at 550 megawatts.
Basin Electric, headquartered in Bismarck. N.D., is the operator of LRS and majority owner with a 42.27 percent stake. Five other Midwest public utilities co-own the plant.
